manifest.title: Gaifman's Theorem

inputs.abstract:
This submission formalizes Gaifman's normal-form theorem for first-order
logic over finite relational vocabularies. It develops the syntax and
semantics of relational structures and first-order formulas, the associated
Gaifman graph and its metric neighborhoods, local formulas, and uniform basic
local sentences.

The main result states that every first-order formula is equivalent to a
Boolean combination of formulas local around its free variables and vocabulary
constants, and sentences asserting the existence of pairwise distant witnesses
satisfying one fixed local formula. In the sentence case every constituent is
closed by construction. Each constituent records its own radius, and all such
radii satisfy the theorem's uniform exponential bound. The formalization
follows Gaifman's original theorem and the formulation in Libkin's *Elements
of Finite Model Theory*.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax512892.RelationalStructures

/-!
---
title: First-order logic over a relational vocabulary
type: definition
---
First-order terms are variables or constants. Formulas are relation atoms,
equalities, negations, disjunctions, and existential quantifications. The
satisfaction relation gives these constructors their usual semantics, and the
quantifier rank is the greatest nesting depth of quantifiers.

# Formalization notes

`Formula σ k` has exactly `k` available free variables. Variables are finite
levels: an existential quantifier adds the new last variable, and satisfaction
extends an environment with `Fin.snoc`. Consequently a sentence has type
`Formula σ 0`; closedness is enforced by the type rather than checked by a
separate predicate. Conjunction and universal quantification are definable from
the chosen constructors and do not need additional semantic cases.
-/

namespace Lax512892.FirstOrder

open Lax512892.RelationalStructures

/-- Terms over `σ` with `k` available variables. -/
inductive Term (σ : Vocabulary) (k : ℕ) : Type
  /-- A variable. -/
  | var (i : Fin k)
  /-- A constant of the vocabulary. -/
  | const (c : σ.Constant)

/-- First-order formulas over `σ` with `k` available free variables. -/
inductive Formula (σ : Vocabulary) : ℕ → Type
  /-- A relation atom. -/
  | rel {k : ℕ} (R : σ.Relation) (args : Fin (σ.arity R) → Term σ k) : Formula σ k
  /-- Equality of terms. -/
  | eq {k : ℕ} (left right : Term σ k) : Formula σ k
  /-- Negation. -/
  | not {k : ℕ} (φ : Formula σ k) : Formula σ k
  /-- Disjunction. -/
  | or {k : ℕ} (φ ψ : Formula σ k) : Formula σ k
  /-- Existential quantification, binding the new last variable. -/
  | ex {k : ℕ} (φ : Formula σ (k + 1)) : Formula σ k

namespace Term

/-- Interpretation of a term in a structure under an environment. -/
def eval {σ : Vocabulary} {M : Type*} {k : ℕ} (A : Structure σ M)
    (env : Fin k → M) : Term σ k → M
  | .var i => env i
  | .const c => A.constant c

end Term

namespace Formula

/-- Satisfaction of a formula in a structure under an environment for its free
variables. -/
def Sat {σ : Vocabulary} {M : Type*} (A : Structure σ M) :
    {k : ℕ} → Formula σ k → (Fin k → M) → Prop
  | _, .rel R args, env => A.relation R (fun i => (args i).eval A env)
  | _, .eq left right, env => left.eval A env = right.eval A env
  | _, .not φ, env => ¬ Sat A φ env
  | _, .or φ ψ, env => Sat A φ env ∨ Sat A ψ env
  | _, .ex φ, env => ∃ x : M, Sat A φ (Fin.snoc env x)

/-- The quantifier rank of a formula. -/
def quantifierRank {σ : Vocabulary} : {k : ℕ} → Formula σ k → ℕ
  | _, .rel _ _ => 0
  | _, .eq _ _ => 0
  | _, .not φ => quantifierRank φ
  | _, .or φ ψ => max (quantifierRank φ) (quantifierRank ψ)
  | _, .ex φ => quantifierRank φ + 1

end Formula

end Lax512892.FirstOrder

concepts.title: Gaifman's normal-form theorem
concepts.description:
Every first-order formula over a finite relational vocabulary has an effective,
uniform translation into a Boolean combination of formulas local around its
free tuple and basic local sentences. At radius `r`, a basic local sentence
asserts that there are `s` witnesses, pairwise at Gaifman distance greater than
`2r`, all satisfying the same one-variable `r`-local formula.

If the input has quantifier rank `q` and `k` free variables, the radius can be
chosen at most `7^q`, and every basic local sentence needs at most `q + k`
witnesses. When the input is a sentence, every constituent of the normal form
is itself a sentence. This closedness condition is enforced by the index of
`NormalForm`: a value of type `NormalForm σ 0` can contain only zero-anchor
local formulas and basic local sentences. The equivalence is over all finite
structures.

This is the uniform formulation of Gaifman's theorem used in Theorem 4.22 of
Libkin's *Elements of Finite Model Theory*, following Gaifman's original
locality theorem.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The output syntax is reified. `NormalForm σ k` is a Boolean combination whose
atoms are either local formulas around the `k` free variables or basic local
sentences; every atom records its own radius. This permits the uniform radius
bound and the witness bound to be stated directly about every atom that occurs,
without incorrectly requiring unrelated constituents to use one common radius.
In the sentence case `k = 0`, closedness follows from the syntax rather than
from excluding zero-anchor local formulas; such closed local formulas are
needed, for example, to express quantifier-free facts about constants or
nullary relations.

The theorem quantifies once over a single translation function, before any
input formula or structure. This records uniformity more faithfully than a
separate existential normal form for each formula. It does not assert a running
time bound for the translation. A constructive proof of the axiom supplies the
effective transformation; code extraction is not part of the concept surface.

The `s = 0` basic sentence is allowed and is vacuously true, exactly as the
displayed first-order sentence with an empty witness tuple. Pairwise separation
is imposed only for distinct witness indices.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax512892.Locality
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Basic

/-!
---
title: Gaifman's normal-form theorem
type: theorem
---
Every first-order formula over a finite relational vocabulary has an effective,
uniform translation into a Boolean combination of formulas local around its
free tuple and basic local sentences. At radius `r`, a basic local sentence
asserts that there are `s` witnesses, pairwise at Gaifman distance greater than
`2r`, all satisfying the same one-variable `r`-local formula.

If the input has quantifier rank `q` and `k` free variables, the radius can be
chosen at most `7^q`, and every basic local sentence needs at most `q + k`
witnesses. When the input is a sentence, every constituent of the normal form
is itself a sentence. This closedness condition is enforced by the index of
`NormalForm`: a value of type `NormalForm σ 0` can contain only zero-anchor
local formulas and basic local sentences. The equivalence is over all finite
structures.

This is the uniform formulation of Gaifman's theorem used in Theorem 4.22 of
Libkin's *Elements of Finite Model Theory*, following Gaifman's original
locality theorem.

# Formalization notes

The output syntax is reified. `NormalForm σ k` is a Boolean combination whose
atoms are either local formulas around the `k` free variables or basic local
sentences; every atom records its own radius. This permits the uniform radius
bound and the witness bound to be stated directly about every atom that occurs,
without incorrectly requiring unrelated constituents to use one common radius.
In the sentence case `k = 0`, closedness follows from the syntax rather than
from excluding zero-anchor local formulas; such closed local formulas are
needed, for example, to express quantifier-free facts about constants or
nullary relations.

The theorem quantifies once over a single translation function, before any
input formula or structure. This records uniformity more faithfully than a
separate existential normal form for each formula. It does not assert a running
time bound for the translation. A constructive proof of the axiom supplies the
effective transformation; code extraction is not part of the concept surface.

The `s = 0` basic sentence is allowed and is vacuously true, exactly as the
displayed first-order sentence with an empty witness tuple. Pairwise separation
is imposed only for distinct witness indices.
-/

namespace Lax512892.GaifmanNormalForm

open Lax512892.RelationalStructures Lax512892.FirstOrder Lax512892.Locality

universe u

/-- Boolean combinations of atoms of type `α`. -/
inductive BooleanCombination (α : Type u) : Type u
  /-- An atomic constituent. -/
  | atom (a : α)
  /-- Truth, serving also as the empty Boolean combination. -/
  | truth
  /-- Negation. -/
  | not (b : BooleanCombination α)
  /-- Conjunction. -/
  | and (b c : BooleanCombination α)

namespace BooleanCombination

/-- Evaluation of a Boolean combination from an interpretation of its atoms. -/
def eval {α : Type u} (value : α → Prop) : BooleanCombination α → Prop
  | .atom a => value a
  | .truth => True
  | .not b => ¬ b.eval value
  | .and b c => b.eval value ∧ c.eval value

/-- The atoms occurring in a Boolean combination, with multiplicity. -/
def atoms {α : Type u} : BooleanCombination α → List α
  | .atom a => [a]
  | .truth => []
  | .not b => b.atoms
  | .and b c => b.atoms ++ c.atoms

end BooleanCombination

/-- A basic local sentence at radius `r`: `witnessCount` pairwise far-apart
witnesses all satisfy the same one-variable local formula `property`. -/
structure BasicLocalSentence (σ : Vocabulary) (r : ℕ) where
  /-- The number of witnesses. -/
  witnessCount : ℕ
  /-- The uniform local property required of every witness. -/
  property : LocalFormula σ 1 r 0

namespace BasicLocalSentence

/-- Semantics of a basic local sentence. -/
def Sat {σ : Vocabulary} {M : Type*} {r : ℕ} (A : Structure σ M)
    (β : BasicLocalSentence σ r) : Prop :=
  ∃ witnesses : Fin β.witnessCount → M,
    (∀ i, β.property.Sat A (fun _ => witnesses i) Fin.elim0) ∧
      ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
        ¬ distanceAtMost A (2 * r) (witnesses i) (witnesses j)

end BasicLocalSentence

/-- An atom of a Gaifman normal form. Each atom carries its own locality
radius. -/
inductive NormalAtom (σ : Vocabulary) (k : ℕ) : Type
  /-- A formula local around the `k` free variables. -/
  | local (r : ℕ) (formula : LocalFormula σ k r 0)
  /-- A basic local sentence. -/
  | basic (r : ℕ) (sentence : BasicLocalSentence σ r)

/-- A Gaifman normal form for a formula with `k` free variables. -/
structure NormalForm (σ : Vocabulary) (k : ℕ) where
  /-- A Boolean combination of local formulas and basic local sentences. -/
  body : BooleanCombination (NormalAtom σ k)

namespace NormalForm

/-- Satisfaction of a normal form under an environment for its free variables. -/
def Sat {σ : Vocabulary} {M : Type*} {k : ℕ} (A : Structure σ M)
    (env : Fin k → M) (nf : NormalForm σ k) : Prop :=
  nf.body.eval fun atom =>
    match atom with
    | .local _ ψ => ψ.Sat A env Fin.elim0
    | .basic _ basic => basic.Sat A

/-- Every constituent occurring in `nf` has radius at most `bound`. -/
def RadiiBounded {σ : Vocabulary} {k : ℕ}
    (nf : NormalForm σ k) (bound : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ atom : NormalAtom σ k, atom ∈ nf.body.atoms →
    match atom with
    | .local r _ => r ≤ bound
    | .basic r _ => r ≤ bound

/-- Every basic local sentence occurring in `nf` uses at most `bound`
witnesses. -/
def WitnessesBounded {σ : Vocabulary} {k : ℕ}
    (nf : NormalForm σ k) (bound : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (r : ℕ) (basic : BasicLocalSentence σ r),
    NormalAtom.basic r basic ∈ nf.body.atoms → basic.witnessCount ≤ bound

end NormalForm

/-- **Gaifman's normal-form theorem.** There is a uniform transformation of
every first-order formula over `σ` into an equivalent Gaifman normal form. For
an input of quantifier rank `q` with `k` free variables, every constituent has
radius at most `7 ^ q`, and each basic local sentence has at most `q + k`
witnesses. If the input is a sentence, the result has type `NormalForm σ 0`, so
every constituent is closed. Equivalence holds in every finite `σ`-structure. -/
axiom gaifmanNormalForm (σ : Vocabulary) :
    ∃ translate : (k : ℕ) → Formula σ k → NormalForm σ k,
      ∀ (k : ℕ) (φ : Formula σ k),
        (translate k φ).RadiiBounded (7 ^ φ.quantifierRank) ∧
        (translate k φ).WitnessesBounded (φ.quantifierRank + k) ∧
        ∀ {M : Type} [Fintype M] (A : Structure σ M) (env : Fin k → M),
          φ.Sat A env ↔ (translate k φ).Sat A env

end Lax512892.GaifmanNormalForm

statements.signature:
gaifmanNormalForm : ∀ (σ : Lax512892.RelationalStructures.Vocabulary),
  Exists fun translate =>
    ∀ (k : Nat) (φ : Lax512892.FirstOrder.Formula σ k),
      And ((translate k φ).RadiiBounded (instHPow.hPow 7 φ.quantifierRank))
        (And ((translate k φ).WitnessesBounded (instHAdd.hAdd φ.quantifierRank k))
          (∀ {M : Type} [Fintype M] (A : Lax512892.RelationalStructures.Structure σ M) (env : Fin k → M),
            Iff (Lax512892.FirstOrder.Formula.Sat A φ env)
              (Lax512892.GaifmanNormalForm.NormalForm.Sat A env (translate k φ))))

concepts.title: Gaifman distance and local formulas
concepts.description:
Two distinct elements of a relational structure are Gaifman-adjacent when they
occur together in a tuple belonging to an interpreted relation. The predicate
`distanceAtMost A r a b` says that the Gaifman graph has a walk of length at
most `r` from `a` to `b`.

An `r`-local formula around a tuple of anchor variables is represented by a
syntax in which every quantifier is explicitly restricted to the union of the
radius-`r` balls around those anchors and around the interpretations of all
vocabulary constants. Its atomic terms may refer to anchors, locally bound
variables, and vocabulary constants. This is the syntactic notion of locality
used by Gaifman's normal-form theorem, not merely a semantic invariance
property.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Anchor variables and locally bound variables have separate types. This prevents
a newly quantified variable from silently becoming an additional centre of the
neighbourhood. The semantics of the local existential constructor chooses an
element in the ball around one of the original anchors or a vocabulary constant
and extends only the bound-variable environment. Negation supplies restricted
universal quantification in the usual way. Including constants as centres is
the extension made immediately before Theorem 4.22 in Libkin's *Elements of
Finite Model Theory*.

Distance is defined by bounded walks instead of a minimum taking the value
infinity. At radius zero it is equality; the successor clause either uses a
shorter walk or takes one Gaifman edge followed by a shorter walk.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax512892.FirstOrder

/-!
---
title: Gaifman distance and local formulas
type: definition
---
Two distinct elements of a relational structure are Gaifman-adjacent when they
occur together in a tuple belonging to an interpreted relation. The predicate
`distanceAtMost A r a b` says that the Gaifman graph has a walk of length at
most `r` from `a` to `b`.

An `r`-local formula around a tuple of anchor variables is represented by a
syntax in which every quantifier is explicitly restricted to the union of the
radius-`r` balls around those anchors and around the interpretations of all
vocabulary constants. Its atomic terms may refer to anchors, locally bound
variables, and vocabulary constants. This is the syntactic notion of locality
used by Gaifman's normal-form theorem, not merely a semantic invariance
property.

# Formalization notes

Anchor variables and locally bound variables have separate types. This prevents
a newly quantified variable from silently becoming an additional centre of the
neighbourhood. The semantics of the local existential constructor chooses an
element in the ball around one of the original anchors or a vocabulary constant
and extends only the bound-variable environment. Negation supplies restricted
universal quantification in the usual way. Including constants as centres is
the extension made immediately before Theorem 4.22 in Libkin's *Elements of
Finite Model Theory*.

Distance is defined by bounded walks instead of a minimum taking the value
infinity. At radius zero it is equality; the successor clause either uses a
shorter walk or takes one Gaifman edge followed by a shorter walk.
-/

namespace Lax512892.Locality

open Lax512892.RelationalStructures Lax512892.FirstOrder

/-- Adjacency in the Gaifman graph of a relational structure. -/
def gaifmanAdjacent {σ : Vocabulary} {M : Type*} (A : Structure σ M) (a b : M) : Prop :=
  a ≠ b ∧
    ∃ (R : σ.Relation) (tuple : Fin (σ.arity R) → M),
      A.relation R tuple ∧
        ∃ i j : Fin (σ.arity R), i ≠ j ∧ tuple i = a ∧ tuple j = b

/-- `distanceAtMost A r a b` holds when a walk of at most `r` Gaifman edges
joins `a` to `b`. -/
def distanceAtMost {σ : Vocabulary} {M : Type*} (A : Structure σ M) :
    ℕ → M → M → Prop
  | 0, a, b => a = b
  | r + 1, a, b =>
      distanceAtMost A r a b ∨
        ∃ c : M, gaifmanAdjacent A a c ∧ distanceAtMost A r c b

/-- Membership in the union of the radius-`r` balls around `anchors` and the
interpretations of all vocabulary constants. -/
def inBallAround {σ : Vocabulary} {M : Type*} (A : Structure σ M)
    (r : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (anchors : Fin k → M) (x : M) : Prop :=
  (∃ i : Fin k, distanceAtMost A r (anchors i) x) ∨
    ∃ c : σ.Constant, distanceAtMost A r (A.constant c) x

/-- A term in a local formula, distinguishing the fixed anchor variables from
variables introduced by restricted quantifiers. -/
inductive LocalTerm (σ : Vocabulary) (anchorCount boundCount : ℕ) : Type
  /-- One of the fixed variables around which locality is measured. -/
  | anchor (i : Fin anchorCount)
  /-- A variable introduced by a restricted quantifier. -/
  | bound (i : Fin boundCount)
  /-- A constant of the vocabulary. -/
  | const (c : σ.Constant)

/-- Formulas whose quantifiers are all restricted to the radius-`r` balls
around the original `anchorCount` variables and the vocabulary constants. -/
inductive LocalFormula (σ : Vocabulary) (anchorCount r : ℕ) : ℕ → Type
  /-- A relation atom. -/
  | rel {boundCount : ℕ} (R : σ.Relation)
      (args : Fin (σ.arity R) → LocalTerm σ anchorCount boundCount) :
      LocalFormula σ anchorCount r boundCount
  /-- Equality of local terms. -/
  | eq {boundCount : ℕ} (left right : LocalTerm σ anchorCount boundCount) :
      LocalFormula σ anchorCount r boundCount
  /-- Negation. -/
  | not {boundCount : ℕ} (φ : LocalFormula σ anchorCount r boundCount) :
      LocalFormula σ anchorCount r boundCount
  /-- Disjunction. -/
  | or {boundCount : ℕ} (φ ψ : LocalFormula σ anchorCount r boundCount) :
      LocalFormula σ anchorCount r boundCount
  /-- Existential quantification restricted to the radius-`r` balls around the
  original anchors and the vocabulary constants. -/
  | ex {boundCount : ℕ} (φ : LocalFormula σ anchorCount r (boundCount + 1)) :
      LocalFormula σ anchorCount r boundCount

namespace LocalTerm

/-- Interpretation of a term occurring in a local formula. -/
def eval {σ : Vocabulary} {M : Type*} {anchorCount boundCount : ℕ}
    (A : Structure σ M)
    (anchors : Fin anchorCount → M) (bound : Fin boundCount → M) :
    LocalTerm σ anchorCount boundCount → M
  | .anchor i => anchors i
  | .bound i => bound i
  | .const c => A.constant c

end LocalTerm

namespace LocalFormula

/-- Satisfaction for a syntactically local formula. Every existential witness
is required to lie in the fixed neighbourhood of the anchor tuple. -/
def Sat {σ : Vocabulary} {M : Type*} {anchorCount r : ℕ}
    (A : Structure σ M)
    (anchors : Fin anchorCount → M) :
    {boundCount : ℕ} → LocalFormula σ anchorCount r boundCount →
      (Fin boundCount → M) → Prop
  | _, .rel R args, bound =>
      A.relation R (fun i => (args i).eval A anchors bound)
  | _, .eq left right, bound =>
      left.eval A anchors bound = right.eval A anchors bound
  | _, .not φ, bound => ¬ Sat A anchors φ bound
  | _, .or φ ψ, bound => Sat A anchors φ bound ∨ Sat A anchors ψ bound
  | _, .ex φ, bound =>
      ∃ x : M, inBallAround A r anchors x ∧ Sat A anchors φ (Fin.snoc bound x)

end LocalFormula

end Lax512892.Locality

concepts.title: Finite relational vocabularies and structures
concepts.description:
A finite relational vocabulary consists of finitely many relation symbols, each
with a specified finite arity, and finitely many constant symbols. A structure
interprets every relation symbol as a relation of the corresponding arity and
every constant symbol as an element of its carrier.

This is the notion of relational vocabulary used in the stated version of
Gaifman's theorem. Function symbols of positive arity are deliberately absent.
The theorem will quantify over finite carrier types, while the definitions in
this file make sense over any carrier type.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The relation symbols are positions in `relationArities`; the entry at a position
is that symbol's arity. Thus finiteness is built into the type of a vocabulary,
rather than imposed by a typeclass side condition. Constants are represented by
`Fin constantCount`. A structure on an empty carrier can exist exactly when the
vocabulary has no constants, matching the usual convention.

concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Data.Fin.Tuple.Basic

/-!
---
title: Finite relational vocabularies and structures
type: definition
---
A finite relational vocabulary consists of finitely many relation symbols, each
with a specified finite arity, and finitely many constant symbols. A structure
interprets every relation symbol as a relation of the corresponding arity and
every constant symbol as an element of its carrier.

This is the notion of relational vocabulary used in the stated version of
Gaifman's theorem. Function symbols of positive arity are deliberately absent.
The theorem will quantify over finite carrier types, while the definitions in
this file make sense over any carrier type.

# Formalization notes

The relation symbols are positions in `relationArities`; the entry at a position
is that symbol's arity. Thus finiteness is built into the type of a vocabulary,
rather than imposed by a typeclass side condition. Constants are represented by
`Fin constantCount`. A structure on an empty carrier can exist exactly when the
vocabulary has no constants, matching the usual convention.
-/

namespace Lax512892.RelationalStructures

/-- A finite relational vocabulary: a finite list of relation arities and a
finite number of constant symbols. -/
structure Vocabulary where
  /-- One arity for each relation symbol. -/
  relationArities : List ℕ
  /-- The number of constant symbols. -/
  constantCount : ℕ

namespace Vocabulary

/-- The finite type of relation symbols of `σ`. -/
abbrev Relation (σ : Vocabulary) := Fin σ.relationArities.length

/-- The arity of a relation symbol. -/
def arity (σ : Vocabulary) (R : σ.Relation) : ℕ :=
  σ.relationArities.get R

/-- The finite type of constant symbols of `σ`. -/
abbrev Constant (σ : Vocabulary) := Fin σ.constantCount

end Vocabulary

/-- An interpretation of the relational vocabulary `σ` on the carrier `M`. -/
structure Structure (σ : Vocabulary) (M : Type*) where
  /-- Interpretation of every relation symbol as a relation of its arity. -/
  relation : (R : σ.Relation) → (Fin (σ.arity R) → M) → Prop
  /-- Interpretation of every constant symbol. -/
  constant : σ.Constant → M

end Lax512892.RelationalStructures

proofs.description:
Constructive proof of Gaifman's normal-form theorem, using the finite scatter
argument and the stronger intermediate radius bound `7^q - 1`.
